# ExpressionParser.parse() on each, in en_US (ExpressionParserDumper.java writes the results to
# tests/core/util/ExpressionParserParityCases.h). See README.md.
#
# One input per line: <comparison> [<input>], the input between the first "[" and the last "]".
# <comparison> says how the test compares QtRocket's result with OpenRocket's (CLAUDE.md, Portability):
#   =  exactly (+ - * / %, the parsing of numbers, abs, ceil, floor, round, sqrt; a NaN as any NaN)
#   ~  within a tolerance: ^ (Math.pow) or a transcendental function is involved
#   ?  only whether it parses: random()
# Escapes in the input: \t, \n, \r, \\ and \uXXXX (a UTF-16 code unit; a character beyond U+FFFF
# is its surrogate pair). Every other character is itself (printable ASCII only).
